--- order: 4 unit: boxes moveId: box-model reviews: [block-inline] introduces: [box] assumes: [div-span, display, heading, paragraph, image, style-block, css-rule, text-colour, class, class-selector] title: Boxes summary: See every element as a box with padding, a border and a margin, and find out that width sets only the content. language: html app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-html" 8129 url: http://127.0.0.1:8129/index.html ready: HTML code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 40 explainPicture: { ref: page.html#explain, inspect: ".card" } voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } explainClip: query: { code: "@page.html#explain-start", inspect: ".card", zoom: 1.4 } caption: "Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin" clip: - caption: text: "Every element is a box. Box model view shows its parts. The words are the content (blue)." say: "Every element is a box. The words in the middle, in blue, are its content." - wait: 1800 - caption: "padding (green) adds space inside, around the content." - type: { into: HTML code, text: " padding: 20px;\n", after: ".card {\n" } - caption: "border (gold) is the line around the padding." - type: { into: HTML code, text: " border: 5px solid navy;\n", after: "padding: 20px;\n" } - caption: "margin (orange) is space outside the border, between boxes." - type: { into: HTML code, text: " margin: 20px;\n", after: "solid navy;\n" } - caption: text: "width sets the content only: 200 + 20 + 20 + 5 + 5 = 250 wide." say: "Width sets the content only, so with padding and border the box is 250 wide." - type: { into: HTML code, text: " width: 200px;\n", after: "margin: 20px;\n" } - expect: { selector: "#preview-text", contains: "Owls: 12 points" } - wait: 2500 hook: "Look closely at a card on any website: it's a box inside a box inside a box. How big is it, really?" --- Every element on a page is a **box**, and CSS sets how much room each box has inside it and around it. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#card insight: "Most students say 200; the card is 250 because padding and border are added to the width on both sides." check: type: predict q: "How wide is the card on the page, from the outside of its border on the left to the outside on the right, in pixels?" kind: number fault: logic misconception: width-includes-padding actual: "250: 200 for the content, plus 20 padding on each side, plus 5 border on each side." ``` `width` sets how wide a box is, `padding` adds space inside its border, and `border` draws the line. How wide do you think the whole card is? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#card try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#card", height: 400, boxmodel: true } insight: "The Box model view measures each part: content, padding, border and margin." check: { type: reflect, text: "I can say which part of the box is the padding, which is the border, and why the card is wider than its width." } unlocks: [card-box] ``` The **Box model** view is on: point at the card. Blue is the content, green the padding, gold the border, and the label shows the sizes. Compare the width with your prediction. Then change `padding` to `40px` and point at it again, and add `margin: 20px;` to see the orange margin. | Code | What it does | Why | |---|---|---| | `width: 200px;` | Sets how wide the content is | It sets only the words' area. Padding and border are added outside it, on both sides, so the card is wider than 200 | | `padding: 20px;` | Adds room inside the border, around the content | It is part of the box, so the background colour fills it. 20 on each side adds 40 | | `border: 5px solid navy;` | Draws a line around the padding | Thickness, style and colour in one line. 5 on each side adds 10 | | `margin: 20px;` | Adds space outside the border, between boxes | It is outside the box, so it is not part of the card's width and has no background | | `20px` with its `px` | Every size needs a unit | Without one, such as `padding: 20;`, the browser ignores the line and shows no error | ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#cards picture: { ref: page.html#cards, inspect: ".card" } insight: "The width is only the content: padding and border add to it on both sides, and margin is outside it." tasks: - check: type: number q: "In the picture, how wide is the first card on the page, outside border to outside border, in pixels?" answer: 218 fault: logic misconception: width-includes-padding feedback: - [180, "That is only the content. Add the padding and the border on both sides."] - [210, "That adds the padding (15 + 15) but not the border. The border has two sides too."] - [250, "That adds the margin. The margin is outside the card, so it is not part of its width."] explain: "180 for the content, plus 15 + 15 of padding, plus 4 + 4 of border: 218. The 16px margin is outside the card." - picture: { ref: page.html#cards, inspect: ".card" } check: type: question q: "The words touch the border of a card. Which property gives them room inside the border?" options: ["padding", "margin", "width", "background-color"] answer: 0 explain: "Padding is the room between the words and the border. Margin is the space outside the border, between cards." - check: type: bug code: page.html#nounit answer: 3 fault: syntax misconception: css-missing-unit text: "The border shows, but the words are squashed against it: the padding does nothing, and there is no error. Click the line that causes it." explain: "Line 3 has no unit. padding: 20 means nothing to the browser, so it ignores the whole line. It needs padding: 20px;." ``` The picture shows the first card in the **Box model** view: orange margin, gold border, green padding, blue content. ### Add up the width The first card's rule is `width: 180px; padding: 15px; border: 4px solid teal; margin: 16px;`. ### Room for the words The words are squashed against the border. ### The padding that does nothing This card should have room inside its border. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Building a card one property at a time, checking each change with the Box model view." try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#modify", height: 440, boxmodel: true } tasks: - hint: "Add padding: 12px; inside the .card rule." check: { type: code, text: "Give the cards 12px of padding.", rules: { contains: ["padding: 12px;"] } } expected: page.html#sol-padding - hint: "Margin is outside the border: margin: 16px;" check: { type: code, text: "Space the cards apart with 16px of margin.", rules: { contains: ["margin: 16px;"] } } expected: page.html#sol-margin - hint: "width: 200px; Remember that padding and border are added to it." check: { type: code, text: "Make each card's content 200px wide.", rules: { contains: ["width: 200px;"] } } expected: page.html#sol-width ``` ### Room inside Give the cards `12px` of padding. ### Space between Space the cards apart with `16px` of margin. ### A set width Make each card's content `200px` wide. How wide is each card now? Point at it to check. ## Mix it up ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#review insight: "A span is inline, so its width is ignored until display: block makes it a block box." check: type: question q: "Both tags should be boxes 120px wide, but each is only as wide as its word. The padding works, the width does not. What fixes the width?" options: - "Add display: block; to the .tag rule, because an inline box ignores its width" - "Add more padding, because padding sets the width of an inline box" - "Add a margin, because inline boxes need space around them" - "Change span to p in the CSS, because width belongs to paragraphs" answer: 0 shuffle: false fault: logic misconception: inline-ignores-width feedback: - null - "Padding adds room around the words, but it does not set the width. The width is the part being ignored." - "A margin is space outside the box. It cannot give an inline box a width." - "The CSS rule is for the class .tag, and the tag in the HTML is the span. The span is inline, and that is what ignores the width." explain: "A span is an inline box: it sits in the line of text and ignores width. display: block makes it a block box, so the 120px applies (and each tag then starts a new line)." ``` Both tags are `span` elements in one line of text. ## Make ```step stage: make try: { playground: html, starter: "page.html#make", height: 460, boxmodel: true } hint: - "A card is one box that holds the heading, the picture and the line of text. ``` ```teacher summary: Students see every element as a box of content, padding, border and margin, and find out that width sets only the content, so padding and border make the box wider. time: 45 timing: "Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 12 min · Mix it up 4 min · Modify 8 min · Make 11 min" goals: - "I can name the four parts of a box: content, padding, border and margin." - I can work out how wide a box is from its width, padding and border. - I can use padding and margin to space boxes inside and out. - I can explain why a value without a unit does nothing. before: | Read the unit primer "CSS in 5 minutes" (the box paragraph), then make the Make task's card yourself and point at it with **Box model** on. The **Box model** view (a button in the HTML playground) works like the browser's developer tools: point at any box to see its margin (orange), border (gold), padding (green) and content (blue), with sizes. It never changes the page. The **Boxes** button is different: it adds space to show nesting, so use Box model in this lesson. The one idea: `width` sets the content only. The box on the page is the width plus the padding and border on both sides. Real sites often set `box-sizing: border-box` so that width includes padding and border; mention it once, after students are comfortable with the sums. running: - "Predict: almost everyone says 200. The card is 250 wide: padding and border are added to the width on both sides. Let students check with Box model. Most will say 200. Ask what the 20 and the 5 in the rule are for, then let them point at the card with Box model." - "Run: change the padding and point again. Ask: which number in the label changed, and which part of the card grew?" - "Investigate: the number task is the sum on paper (180 + 30 + 8). The wrong answers are the real slips: content only, one side only, margin included. The last task is `padding: 20` with no unit; the browser ignores it without an error." - "Mix it up: padding works on an inline span but width does not. Ask who remembers what block and inline meant." - "Modify: build the card one property at a time, checking each with Box model, and work out the width before pointing." stuck: - see: Padding or margin does nothing, and there is no error. ask: Does the value have a unit, such as px? fix: "Write padding: 20px; not padding: 20;" - see: The card is wider than the width they set. ask: What else is added to the width? fix: Padding and border are added on both sides; take them into account, or reduce the width. - see: The cards touch each other. ask: Which property makes space outside a box? fix: Add margin to the card's rule (padding is inside the border). stretch: "Use different padding on each side (padding: 10px 30px;) and predict the width before pointing at it. Then add border-radius: 12px; for rounded corners." support: "Give students the Modify starter with Box model on and ask them only to add padding, then margin, pointing at the card after each." leads: "Next lesson is a review of the unit on a whole newsletter page: reading a longer stylesheet and turning the articles into cards. Class idea: measure a real website's buttons with the browser's developer tools (right-click, Inspect)." exit: q: "A box has width: 300px; padding: 10px; border: 2px solid; How wide is it on the page, and why?" a: "324 pixels: 300 for the content, plus 10 padding on each side (20) and 2 border on each side (4)." explain: | The video and the picture show the same steps, in the **Box model** view: 1. Every element is a box. The words are the **content** (blue). 2. `padding` (green) adds space inside, around the content. 3. `border` (gold) is the line around the padding. 4. `margin` (orange) is space outside the border, between boxes. 5. `width` sets the content only, so this card is 200 + 20 + 20 + 5 + 5 = 250 pixels wide. Every size needs a unit, such as `20px`. Without one, the browser ignores it, with no error message. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-padding step-4#t2: page.html#sol-margin step-4#t3: page.html#sol-width step-6: page.html#sol-make step-7: price.html#sol-tag struggle: "Working out that padding and border add to the width. Ask for the sum on paper first (200 + 20 + 20 + 5 + 5), then check it with Box model." class: activities: - at: end kind: activity title: Measure a neighbour's card minutes: 4 do: | Swap cards with a partner. Without running them, add up the width of the card on paper, then point at it with Box model to check. notes: "Listen for students who add only one side of the padding or border. Ask how many sides a box has left and right." ``` ```code page.html#card
